image_description: A large, white radio telescope dish with a complex lattice support structure (truss work) visible on the back and rim. The dish is mounted on a substantial pedestal structure. Green trees are visible in the foreground at the bottom of the frame, providing scale. The sky is overcast.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous parabolic dish antenna of colossal scale, dwarfing all surrounding structures.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish dominates the frame and appears significantly larger than the tree line at the bottom, consistent with a colossal scale.
The silhouette of the dish exhibits a smooth, continuous concave curvature typical of a paraboloid.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a medium-close shot; the full footprint or 'area spanned' is not visible, only the vertical profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Receiver feed horn at focal point of dish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A central sub-reflector assembly (typical of Cassegrain designs) is suspended by struts in front of the dish center, housing the receiver.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish is connected to a robust pivot mechanism atop a pedestal, allowing for rotation and tilting.
The mechanical joints and bearings visible at the base of the dish imply rotational capability.
The very bottom of the support structure is obscured by the tree line; the foundation itself is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal mesh or solid aluminum panel dish surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The face of the dish appears as a solid, smooth white surface, consistent with painted aluminum panels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Astronomical instrument for detecting radio-frequency emissions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall morphology matches the standard design of a radio telescope.
Inferred from the presence of the alt-azimuth mount and heavy-duty structural supports.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The image has low resolution and slight compression artifacts. The fine details of the truss work blend slightly into the background sky, lacking crisp edge definition, but no structural melting is evident.
The foliage lacks distinct leaf definition, appearing as a textured mass. This is likely due to image resolution/compression rather than AI generation failure, but noted as a quality artifact.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of telescope and rule out misclassification as a satellite dish or radar array.
To verify the 3D consistency of the complex truss work behind the dish and ensure the sub-reflector struts connect logically to the rim.
To check for 'floating' elements where the thin struts holding the feed horn meet the main dish structure.
To assess if the low-resolution texture is natural photographic noise or AI-smearing.

focus_areas: Connectivity of the sub-reflector support struts to the dish rim.
Geometric consistency of the rear truss structure (does it look like a valid engineering lattice?).
Edge sharpness between the white dish and the sky.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'spider' assembly holding the central feed horn. In AI images, these thin struts often fail to connect properly to the dish rim or appear to float. Also, verify that the rear truss structure follows a logical geometric pattern and doesn't melt into random lines.
